summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and prior venous thromboembolism was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in left groin pain. Imaging ruled out fractures, and the pain was attributed to a strain of the left inguinal ligament. She was experiencing a polymyositis flare, evidenced by progressive proximal muscle weakness, elevated CK of 7,310 that trended down to 4,885, and reduced exercise tolerance. Her interstitial lung disease was stable on 3L oxygen at night. No changes were made to her immunosuppressive regimen, and she received her scheduled rituximab dose. Warfarin was held at discharge due to an INR of 3.5, with instructions to take 5mg for the next two days and recheck INR. Given her ongoing weakness, she was discharged to an extended care facility for short-term rehabilitation. Her diabetes remained well controlled, and heart failure was not exacerbated during admission.
